headline_marked: Pioneering artist [[Mustafa Monwar to be laid to rest]] in Banani
headline: Pioneering artist Mustafa Monwar to be laid to rest in Banani
summary: The veteran artist, theatre director, and 'Puppetman of Bangladesh' will be buried in Dhaka's Banani Graveyard on Tuesday afternoon.
details: Mustafa Monwar, a pioneering artist, theatre director, and art researcher known for his groundbreaking work in puppetry, has passed away.
His body will be laid to rest at the Banani Graveyard in Dhaka on Tuesday afternoon following a series of farewells.
The final journey begins at 9am on Tuesday, starting with the first funeral prayers at the Bangladesh Television (BTV) premises.
Between 10:30am and 12:30pm, his body will be taken to the Central Shaheed Minar for people from all walks of life to pay their respects.
A second funeral prayer will be held at the Central Mosque of Dhaka University, followed by a visit to the Faculty of Fine Arts at Dhaka University.
At the Faculty of Fine Arts, colleagues and students will have a half-hour window to bid their last farewell to the veteran teacher.
After these formalities, he will be be laid to rest at the Banani Graveyard on Tuesday afternoon.
The body was ritually bathed at Dhanmondi's Taqwa Mosque and brought to his residence in Dhanmondi on Monday afternoon.

Farewell to the 'Puppetman of Bangladesh'.

Mustafa Monwar, a pioneering artist, theatre director, and art researcher known for his groundbreaking work in puppetry, has passed away.

His body will be laid to rest at the Banani Graveyard in Dhaka on Tuesday afternoon following a series of farewells.

The final journey begins at 9am on Tuesday, starting with the first funeral prayers at the Bangladesh Television (BTV) premises.

Between 10:30am and 12:30pm, his body will be taken to the Central Shaheed Minar for people from all walks of life to pay their respects.

A second funeral prayer will be held at the Central Mosque of Dhaka University, followed by a visit to the Faculty of Fine Arts at Dhaka University.

At the Faculty of Fine Arts, colleagues and students will have a half-hour window to bid their last farewell to the veteran teacher.

After these formalities, he will be be laid to rest at the Banani Graveyard on Tuesday afternoon.

The body was ritually bathed at Dhanmondi's Taqwa Mosque and brought to his residence in Dhanmondi on Monday afternoon.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman: [[Teesta Barrage Master Plan to be implemented]] at any cost
headline: PM Tarique Rahman: Teesta Barrage Master Plan to be implemented at any cost
summary: The Prime Minister outlined a three-step economic recovery strategy and emphasized the implementation of the Teesta Barrage Master Plan during a budget discussion in Parliament.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman stated in the National Parliament on Monday that the government will implement the Teesta Barrage Master Plan as a national priority, regardless of the cost.

During the discussion on the proposed budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year, the PM called for unity among all parties, including the opposition, to build public opinion on matters of national importance.
The government has also initiated plans for a Padma Barrage to store excess monsoon water for use during the dry season, alongside prioritizing water management in the Teesta region.

Describing the proposed budget as 'life-friendly,' the Prime Minister emphasized that it aims to provide relief to people of all classes and professions through a fair, humane, and inclusive economic system.

The budget, presented on June 11, involves an annual expenditure of 9.38 lakh crore BDT. The PM highlighted goals of controlling inflation, restoring banking sector discipline, and increasing investment and employment.

To recover from economic hardship, the government plans a three-step strategy: first, preventing economic decline and ensuring food security; second, reforming revenue and the banking sector; and third, building a competitive, innovation-driven economy.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman emphasized the goal of creating an environment where youth can create their own employment through skill and merit, rather than waiting years for jobs.
The government is also working to recover laundered money, having sent Mutual Legal Assistance Requests to 13 countries and signed over 60 Non-Disclosure Agreements to retrieve assets from abroad.
The PM noted that the government inherited a fragile economy plagued by corruption, looting, and mismanagement, but vowed to tackle these crises with political will and effective policies.
